title: Nvidia Discloses 9.3% Stake in Nebius, Sending Neocloud Stock Soaring
excerpt: A regulatory filing revealed Nvidia holds about 22.26 million shares in the Amsterdam-based AI infrastructure company, mostly through pre-funded warrants from its $2 billion March investment.
body:
• Nvidia disclosed a 9.3% stake in Nebius Group — about 22.26 million shares — in a 13G regulatory filing late Monday, pushing the neocloud stock up as much as 15% on Tuesday.
  • The holding consists of 1.19 million shares held directly and 21.07 million shares via pre-funded warrants tied to Nvidia's $2 billion March investment; the warrants cannot be exercised until September 11.
  • Nebius, formerly part of Russia's Yandex, has emerged as the top-performing neocloud of 2026, with shares up 150% year-to-date and a $27 billion Meta cloud deal bolstering its trajectory.
  • The disclosure comes amid a broader pullback in AI infrastructure stocks, as Meta's plans to sell excess cloud capacity and corporate efforts to cut AI spending — dubbed "tokenmaxxing" — weigh on the sector.

Nvidia disclosed late Monday that it holds a 9.3% stake in Nebius Group, the Amsterdam-based neocloud company, according to a Schedule 13G filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. The filing, which detailed approximately 22.26 million shares in the AI infrastructure provider, sent Nebius stock surging as much as 15% on Tuesday to around $209 per share.

The chipmaker's holding is split between 1.19 million shares held directly and 21.07 million shares held through pre-funded warrants. Those warrants stem from Nvidia's $2 billion investment in Nebius announced in March, when CEO Jensen Huang said the two companies were deepening their partnership to meet "the surging global demand for intelligence." The filing specifies that Nvidia is restricted from exercising or selling the warrant-backed shares until September 11.

A Strategic Bet on AI Infrastructure

The size of the stake should not come as a complete surprise to market watchers. Nvidia first disclosed a smaller position in Nebius in early 2025, when it participated in a $700 million private funding round alongside Accel Partners. The March 2026 investment significantly expanded that position, but because the bulk of it came through pre-funded warrants rather than common stock, the full scale of Nvidia's commitment had not appeared in its quarterly 13F filings.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=aWYuDKbeXuk

Nvidia's strategy of investing in companies that purchase or rent its hardware has drawn scrutiny from AI skeptics, who argue it amounts to financing its own customers. But the approach serves a clear purpose: it locks in demand for future generations of Nvidia's AI processors and diversifies the chipmaker's revenue base beyond a handful of hyperscale cloud customers.

Nebius rival CoreWeave, also backed by Nvidia, saw its stock rise more than 7% on Tuesday in sympathy. Smaller peer IREN gained between 1% and 3%. Nvidia's own shares edged up about 1%, part of a broader rally in semiconductor and AI-related stocks.

The Neocloud Standout

Nebius has established itself as the clear standout among neoclouds — the growing class of companies that provide dedicated cloud computing capacity built around Nvidia's GPUs for AI workloads. Its stock has gained roughly 150% in 2026 and quadrupled over the past 12 months, outpacing CoreWeave's 2% year-to-date gain.

"We are deepening our partnership, scaling the cloud to meet the surging global demand for intelligence."

— Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia

https://x.com/nvidia/status/2079715060197310935

The company's momentum traces back to several catalysts. In March, Nebius struck a cloud-computing agreement with Meta Platforms potentially worth up to $27 billion. Last week, it announced its first senior secured debt facility for approximately $775 million.

Nebius also recently closed its acquisition of AI software maker Eigen AI for about $643 million in cash and stock, and earlier this year acquired agentic search company Tavily for around $400 million.

Citi analysts, who hold a "buy" rating on Nebius with a $287 price target, came away from the company's "Inflection" event in San Francisco last month "more constructive on both the durability of pricing and strategic value of Nebius's expanding software stack." The consensus target compiled by Visible Alpha sits around $276.

Headwinds in the Neocloud Sector

The disclosure arrives at a complicated moment for AI infrastructure stocks. Shares in both Nebius and CoreWeave have retreated from mid-June highs after Meta Platforms announced plans to sell excess cloud computing capacity, raising questions about whether the social media giant will follow through on all of its data center commitments.

A new buzzword — "tokenmaxxing" — has entered the tech lexicon, describing the scramble among companies to rein in soaring AI cloud computing bills. The trend has cast a shadow over the sector's growth assumptions, even as demand for AI processing power continues to expand.

"Smaller peer IREN gained between 1% and 3%."

Nebius, originally the Dutch parent company of Russian internet giant Yandex, was reborn in 2024 after a $5.4 billion deal to divest its Russian assets following Moscow's invasion of Ukraine. Under CEO Arkady Volozh, who publicly criticized the war, the company pivoted to AI cloud infrastructure, retaining about 1,300 engineers and data center assets in Finland, France, and the United States.

What It Means for Investors

For investors in the Indian diaspora tracking AI and semiconductor plays, Nvidia's stake validation underscores the rapid maturation of the neocloud segment — a space where several Indian-origin engineers and executives hold senior roles across companies like CoreWeave and cloud infrastructure providers. The AI infrastructure buildout continues to drive demand for specialized talent, particularly in GPU optimization, data center architecture, and cloud platform engineering — areas where Indian tech professionals are heavily represented in Silicon Valley and beyond.

Looking Ahead

Both Nebius and CoreWeave are scheduled to report earnings in mid-August, which will provide a clearer picture of how neocloud revenue is tracking against the sector's ambitious projections. Nebius's annual recurring revenue is projected to land between $7 billion and $9 billion by year-end — a figure that would represent a dramatic transformation for a company that resumed trading on the Nasdaq less than two years ago.

The September 11 lockup expiry on Nvidia's warrant-backed shares will be another date to watch. Until then, the chipmaker's 9.3% stake remains a strong signal of conviction in Nebius's AI infrastructure model — even as the broader sector navigates a period of recalibration.
